title: Something else
summary: Any other measuring instrument: a short general frame, and free recordings you label yourself.
experience_text: A general frame drawn from all the other lists. You know your instrument best: add free recordings for anything it does that these blocks miss, and tell us what they were.
before_you_start: The instrument, its cables, and the program you normally use, closed for now.
If it is connected by USB: unplug other USB devices you can do without (disks, memory sticks, phones, printers). A keyboard and a mouse may stay.

blocks.label: start
blocks.title: Start the program and connect
steps: Make sure the program is closed (and, for a USB instrument, that it is unplugged).
Start this block (the recording starts now).
Plug the instrument in or switch it on, start the program, and connect.
Wait until the program shows the instrument as ready.
blocks.note: Did the program find the instrument by itself?
blocks.why: How the program finds and greets the instrument is the first thing ChromIQ must repeat.

blocks.label: calibrate
blocks.title: Calibrate
blocks.only_if: If the instrument needs no calibration, record 30 seconds of the program waiting and say so.
steps: Start this block.
Calibrate as the program asks, and wait until it is done.
blocks.note: What did you have to do?
blocks.why: Calibration is usually the simplest command and answer to understand.

blocks.label: typical-job
blocks.title: A typical measurement, saved
steps: Start this block.
Measure the way you always do, to the end.
Save the result in the program under a name you will recognise, and send that file together with the zip.
blocks.note: What did you measure, and the name of the saved file.
blocks.why: A typical job paired with the program's own result is the most useful single recording.

blocks.label: cancel
blocks.title: Cancel during a measurement
steps: Start this block.
Start a measurement and press Cancel or Stop in the program while it runs.
blocks.why: A cancel is an ending ChromIQ must handle cleanly.

blocks.label: refused
blocks.title: A measurement that fails on purpose
steps: Start this block.
Make one measurement fail in a harmless way, read the program's message and answer it.
blocks.note: What did you do, and what did the program say?
blocks.why: How the instrument reports a problem is what ChromIQ must understand.

blocks.label: modes
blocks.title: Every other mode
blocks.only_if: Only the modes your program offers.
steps: Start this block.
For each other mode the program offers, take one measurement.
Before each one, type the mode's name here and press Enter.
blocks.note: The modes you tried, in order.
blocks.why: Each mode may be its own command.

blocks.label: idle
blocks.title: Five quiet minutes
steps: Start this block.
With the program connected and idle, do nothing for five minutes.
blocks.note: Did anything happen on its own?
blocks.why: Programs often keep talking to an idle instrument.

blocks.label: disconnect
blocks.title: Disconnect and reconnect
steps: Start this block (the recording keeps going).
With the program idle, pull the instrument's cable (or switch it off).
Wait 10 seconds, connect it again, and wait until the program shows it again.
blocks.why: A lost connection is an ending ChromIQ must survive.

blocks.label: free
blocks.title: Anything else, labelled by you
steps: Type a short label for what you will record (for example "lamp test").
Start this block and do that one thing in the program.
You can do this block as often as you like, with a new label each time.
blocks.why: You know what your instrument can do; anything we did not think of is welcome.

blocks.label: close
blocks.title: Close the program
steps: Start this block.
Close the program the normal way, and wait 10 seconds.
blocks.why: What the program sends when it closes is what ChromIQ should do when it lets go of the instrument.

blocks.label: unexpected-end
blocks.title: The program ends by force while a measurement, then starts again
steps: Start this block.
Start a measurement in the program.
While it is busy, end the program by force (Windows: Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc), select the program, End task. Mac: Apple menu > Force Quit, select the program, Force Quit.) Type killed.
Wait 20 seconds. Start the program again and note what it does with the instrument (a new calibration, a message).
blocks.note: What did the instrument do when the program disappeared, and when it came back?
blocks.why: After an unexpected end the instrument is left as the program left it; how the maker's program recovers is what ChromIQ needs after its own unexpected end.

blocks.label: questions
blocks.title: A few questions
steps: No recording now. Answer the questions below; a short line each is fine.
questions: Which instrument is it, and what kind (spot, strip, table, sheet reader, something else)?
Which program and which version did you use, on which system?
What else can it do that these blocks did not cover?
blocks.why: The recording cannot say which program made it.
